newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks push ahead in morning, focus on property.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks push ahead in morning, focus on property.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks pushed sharply higher in morning trade on Friday, encouraged by the Hang Seng Index's move above 13,000 points on Thursday and propelled by renewed interest in banking and property stocks, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index surged 80 points, or 0.62 percent, to 13,101. Turnover was HK$2.42 billion after the first half hour of trade.

"The market continues to go up. Banks are better, properties have recovered and selective second- and third-line stocks are also attracting buyers," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.

Brokers said investors were anticipating a bottoming out in local property prices and that property stocks should run up ahead of that. Improved sentiment on the sector helped the market shrug off a 32-point fall overnight in the Dow industrials, which closed at 6,976.
"Developers seem to be very confident about the prospects for the market as they bought lands aggressively and paid huge amounts of money for land premiums to the government," Ng said.
Henderson Land added $0.50 to HK$66.75 and Cheung Kong rose HK$1.00 to HK$70.50.
HSBC Holdings gained HK$1.50 to HK$196.50.
Brokers said the results of the U.K. election should have very limited impact on the local stock market.
"It has no effect, the Labour Party has nothing to do with Hong Kong and there is just about 60 days to go," said Boby Ho, dealing manager at G.K. Goh Securities.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1.
But Ho said the market should be a bit volatile on Friday with profit-taking expected later in the day.
The Hang Seng retreated at mid-morning to 13,051, up 30 points, after touching a high of 13,146. The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index rose 10 points, or 0.90 percent, to 1,084.
Tianjin Bohai surged HK$0.09 to HK$0.98 and Kunming Machine added HK$0.10 to HK$1.17.
Brokers said investors were likely to trade with some caution ahead of the release of U.S. employment data later on Friday.
May Hang Seng Index futures put on 38 points to 13,008 and June added 15 at 13,015.
